data.title: OrthoLite Launches New Supercritical Foam Insole Collection for Performance Footwear at The Running Event 2026
data.description:
OrthoLite Launches New Supercritical Foam Insole Collection for Performance Footwear at The Running Event 2026

OrthoLite®, the global leader in branded, high-performance comfort footwear solutions, introduces OrthoLite® Lift™, a brand new, next-generation insole innovation that delivers lightweight comfort and high resilience by combining engineered polymer formulations with supercritical foaming technology. The new Lift collection will be unveiled at The Running Event in San Antonio, Texas Dec. 1-3, 2026.

The OrthoLite Lift collection uses supercritically foamed aliphatic TPU through a supercritical foaming process, which gives footwear brands and their factory partners a coordinated set of performance options for the footbed. The new OrthoLite Lift innovation shows the material science depth that OrthoLite brings to the industry as part of the Coats Footwear Division.

OrthoLite Lift uses supercritical foaming technology to create a consistent, refined cellular structure, delivering lightweight cushioning and high resilience. Lift expands OrthoLite’s material platform beyond its established open-cell PU technologies, giving brands greater choice in engineering comfort and performance.

Lift debuts with two formulations:

  • OrthoLite® Lift™ ATPU: Built for high-demand environments like trail running, hiking and elite athletic performance, Lift ATPU delivers exceptional lightness in a low-density construction, ≥65% resilience, better step-in comfort and abrasion resistance. Its hydrophobic, closed-cell construction resists water absorption, helping maintain structural integrity and consistent cushioning in dry and wet conditions.
  • OrthoLite® Lift™ DLT: OrthoLite Dual Layer Technology (DLT) combines a supercritically foamed ATPU base for lightweight resilience with a customizable OrthoLite open-cell PU top layer for comfort, breathability and moisture management of the insole. OrthoLite DLT is ideal for all active lifestyle footwear categories.

“Footwear brands aren’t looking for incremental gains anymore. They want material innovation they can build a product and brand story around,” said Marty Greenwald, Vice President of Sales for OrthoLite. “Lift gives brands a new material option when they need lightweight cushioning, high resilience and lasting comfort. And it’s just the latest from an innovation pipeline built on decades of OrthoLite material science.”

Attendees can explore the OrthoLite Lift insole collection at booth #21111 at The Running Event, Dec. 1-3, 2026, in San Antonio. Footwear brands and factory partners can learn more at ortholite.com.

About OrthoLite®

A division of Coats Group plc, OrthoLite® is the world's leading manufacturer and supplier of branded, high-performance, comfort footwear solutions, which the company delivers at scale while prioritizing reduced-impact manufacturing and responsible innovation. Through long-standing partnerships and industry initiatives, OrthoLite supports brands, consumers and the broader footwear ecosystem. Visit www.ortholite.com to learn more.

About Coats Group plc

Coats is a world-leading Tier 2 manufacturer and trusted partner for the apparel and footwear industries. We deliver essential materials, components, and software solutions that help our customers grow, compete and win.

With over 250 years of industry expertise, we’re shaping the future of the apparel and footwear supply chain through insight-led innovation, impactful sustainability practices, and digital technologies that unlock better product quality, efficiency and performance.

Headquartered in the UK, Coats is a FTSE 250 company and a constituent of the FTSE4Good Index. In 2025, we generated $1.5 billion in revenue and employed approximately 19,000 people worldwide – all united by a spirit of innovation, quality and service.

data.title: Webster First CEO highlights financial literacy gap in Worcester Business Journal thought leadership article
data.description:
Webster First CEO highlights financial literacy gap in Worcester Business Journal thought leadership article

Webster First CEO highlights financial literacy gap in Worcester Business Journal thought leadership article

PR Newswire

WORCESTER, Mass., Nov. 20, 2026

WORCESTER, Mass., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Webster First Federal Credit Union announced today that its CEO, John Thomasian, has published a thought leadership article as part of the Worcester Business Journal's Thought Leadership program. The article explores the financial literacy gap affecting young adults across the country and outlines steps Webster First is taking to help close it.

The article points to data from the Forbes Finance Council showing that 80% of U.S. adults never received formal financial education in school, and 88% say high school didn't prepare them to make sound financial decisions. According to Thomasian, this gap leaves many young adults opening their first accounts, taking on their first loans, and making major financial decisions without a solid understanding of credit, interest, budgeting, or long-term saving.

"As a credit union, I believe leaders of financial institutions have a responsibility to offer financial products that align with modern banking needs, but also to educate sound financial advice," Thomasian said. "Community first banking is not just something we say. It's a principle we should live by."

The article emphasizes that the consequences of the financial literacy gap extend well beyond individual households. Today's young adults are tomorrow's entrepreneurs, homeowners, and executives, and without strong financial decision-making skills, the effects ripple out to the broader workforce, economy, and community. "Closing the financial literacy gap is an investment in the future workforce, economy, and our communities," Thomasian said.

To help address this challenge, Webster First has committed to building relationships with schools, parents, and young members through research on youth banking trends, family-focused digital banking products, and a library of free financial literacy resources available to the public. The credit union's Teen Checking account is one practical example of this commitment, giving younger members a debit card and online banking access while allowing parents to set controls on spending and account funding. Financial literacy articles are also built directly into Webster First's mobile app, so parents and teens can learn together.

Thomasian's article also offers guidance for parents looking to support their teens' financial growth, encouraging open conversations about budgeting, saving habits, and the value of small spending decisions over time. Suggested steps include setting specific savings goals with a dollar amount and timeline, building a habit of saving first, and reviewing income and expenses together each month.

Webster First remains committed to preparing the next generation with the financial knowledge and decision-making skills needed to manage money responsibly and build long-term financial stability.

About Webster First Federal Credit Union

Founded in 1928, Webster First Federal Credit Union is one of the largest credit unions in Massachusetts, serving more than 80,000 members and managing nearly $1.5 billion in assets. As a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative, Webster First offers a full suite of personal and business banking products, including checking, savings, loans, and digital banking services, to members in Essex, Middlesex, Suffolk, and Worcester Counties. The credit union has been rated five stars by BauerFinancial for more than eight years and was named among Newsweek's Best Regional Banks and Credit Unions. All deposits are insured up to $250,000 by NCUA, with additional amounts covered by MSIC. For more information, visit websterfirst.com.

data.title: Everyone's making money off 'GTA 6' this week - except investors in Take-Two's stock
data.description:
By Bill Peters

'Grand Theft Auto VI' might be a blockbuster game, but investors are shrugging it off

"Grand Theft Auto VI" finally arrived this week.

Take-Two Interactive's "Grand Theft Auto VI" might be one of the biggest entertainment events ever, but investors haven't been impressed.

Shares of Take-Two (TTWO) - which owns Rockstar Games, the developer of "GTA 6" - are down around 8% over the past five days. While shares rallied on Wednesday, a day before the videogame's official release, they fell Thursday and then seesawed on Friday after official sales figures dropped.

Rockstar Games on Friday said first-day retail sales for the game had hit $3.79 billion. It said 32.5 million units sold pre-release.

"It's partly a sell-the-news moment," said Nick McKay, an analyst who follows the videogame industry at Freedom Capital Markets. "I think it's partly the fact that tech more broadly has been weak of late."

"GTA 6" has earned a near-perfect Metacritic score, drawing praise for its more mature storyline - a present-day Floridian twist on Bonnie and Clyde - and an immersive open-world experience. People have called in sick to spend time playing the game. Boyfriends have disappeared to tend to their in-game girlfriends. Some researchers have anticipated a spike in online food-delivery orders. Others have called the game a reflection of the garbled, unhinged state of the U.S. itself. Analysts, by and large, are optimistic about the game's prospects for years to come.

But McKay noted that "GTA 6" debuted the same week as Anthropic's (ANT) IPO, potentially steering some investors' attention away from the game. More broadly, the AI trade is a mess for multiple reasons, and AI advances, along with the cost-of-living squeeze, have posed a threat to the videogame industry.

Moreover, McKay said, investors and gamers' frustrations with Take-Two may have been building in the months leading up to the game's launch, as details about "GTA 6" remained sparse.

He said that people have been waiting for the game essentially since "Grand Theft Auto V" launched in 2013. But he said there was little news on "GTA 6" until about three months ago, when Netflix (NFLX) offered an extended look at the game in August. The game's release suffered from multiple delays. Ahead of "GTA 6's" debut, hackers also leaked footage of the game, exploiting the information vacuum, he said. Moreover, some data had shown that "NBA 2K27," which is part of Take-Two's other big videogame franchise, had underperformed.

"If we all assumed that 'GTA' would be a very well-reviewed game, and we assumed that it would perform well, you say to yourself, 'OK, well, what comes next?'" McKay said.

"We don't have really any information on when 'GTA's' going to launch on PCs, when 'GTA Online' is going to launch for the new game, so I think investors have started to look toward that," he added.

Shares of Take-Two are down 18.7% so far this year.

Oppenheimer analysts, in a note on Thursday, also suggested the game's realism was both a strength and a weakness.

"The more demanding police encounters, elaborate vehicle interactions, and everyday activities may slow gameplay and sometimes feel too laborious vs. 'GTA V,'" they said.

They also said the gameplay could be cumbersome at times. Clunky controls - for driving, fighting and other actions - "can occasionally break immersion." And they had questions over how any future online version of "GTA 6" might make money off of updates, add-ons and in-game purchases.

Morgan Stanley analysts, in a note on Thursday, said any post-launch press releases on sales figures from Take-Two could also serve as a "sell the news" event for the company's stock. Along with the launch of a PC version of the game, they, too, said investors' attention would soon shift toward how Take-Two and Rockstar can keep online players spending.

"Unlike the initial game purchase, this spending can recur over many years, as demonstrated over 'GTA Online's' 13-year history," they said. "We see the potential combination of a larger audience and higher monetization as an important driver of multi-year earnings growth, with strong launch sales establishing the foundation for the next decade of monetization."

McKay said that some Wall Street analysts who follow videogames were new to the space, and lacked historical context on how games tend to sell. Demand estimates were all over the place, and some were overly optimistic, making it difficult to please everyone, he said.

Sales for "GTA 5," he noted, spiked in the days after it hit shelves, but plateaued in the months after that initial rush. Just because an estimated 130 million to 140 million newer-generation PS5 and Xbox Series X|S consoles are in people's homes doesn't mean that many copies of "GTA 6" will be sold. And he said that few gamers were likely on the fence about whether to buy "GTA 6" at this point.

McKay pointed to other challenges for Take-Two and the rest of the industry. Shifts to digital and mobile gaming remain a threat. Consoles and other hardware are expensive. The industry's growing focus on mega-franchises - like "Grand Theft Auto" or "Call of Duty" - have threatened demand downstream. As those games gobble up more playing hours and dollars, other games can suffer, he said.

"What you see on the console side is games that would have been bigger sellers 10, 15, 20 years ago, when they launch now, the demand isn't there," he said. "Because consumers have said 'You know what? My money's going toward 'Call of Duty' now. Or, my money's going toward 'GTA.'"

-Bill Peters

Picsart Opens the AI Behind Its Platform to Developers & Businesses

With Picsart Platform, developers can build their own video, audio, image features using 250+ models from 30+ providers, alongside Picsart's own editing models, through one API, CLI or MCP server.

Key Takeaways

  • One bundle, four ways to build: the API, the CLI, a playground to test models, and Picsart Media Studio, an MCP server that works with compatible AI assistants.
  • One integration for image, video, audio and text generation from 250+ models across 30+ providers, with the freedom to switch models as a product evolves. Self-serve users pay per generation at competitive, published rates.
  • Developers get access to Picsart's proprietary editing models, like Enhance and background removal, which are only available on Picsart Platform.

Picsart, the AI media production and distribution platform backed by Sequoia Capital and SoftBank Vision Fund 2, today launched Picsart Platform - a multimodal creative AI hub that gives developers the technology behind the platform used by more than 100 million people each month.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120520968/en/

Picsart Opens the AI Behind Its Platform to Developers & Businesses. They can now build their own video, audio, image features using 250+ models from 30+ providers, alongside Picsart's own editing models, through one API, CLI or MCP server.

As new video and image models launch every few weeks, managing separate APIs, API keys, and billing systems creates a fragmented ecosystem. By offering unified access to creative tools, Picsart Platform eliminates fragmentation for all creators, spanning independent developers and corporate marketing teams and studios, by providing access to over 250 video, audio, image, and text models across 30+ providers through a unified integration. Picsart provides access to the latest models at launch, so users can try the newest one without rebuilding.

Developers can switch video models without rewriting their integration, and they can use Picsart's editing models to refine images before or after generation. Developers can access the entire catalog via REST API, Python and TypeScript SDKs, a CLI, or an MCP server. As teams increasingly rely on AI coding agents, having access to an MCP server becomes essential for seamless development.

Hovhannes Avoyan, Founder and CEO of Picsart, says: "Generative media is moving faster than any team can integrate it, our job is to keep up so our customers don't have to. Picsart Platform puts the newest creative AI models and Picsart's own editing tools within reach for solo developers, entrepreneurs and the enterprises we're increasingly built to serve. A two-person startup and a global brand should have access to the same creative engine."

Launch Offer and Availability

Picsart Platform is officially live today. New users can access unlimited Wan 3.0 via Picsart Platform from November 20–22, there will also be an opportunity to receive bonus credits while the promotional pool remains available.

Get your API key at picsart.com/api-platform.

About Picsart

Picsart is the AI-powered platform built for a content-first world. For more than 14 years, it has empowered the next generation of storytellers to create, scale and now monetize video content. Combining intuitive design tools, AI-powered image and video creation, and MCP and CLI functions, Picsart meets creators wherever they work. With more than 100 million monthly active users and over 2.5 billion downloads to date, Picsart is powering a new era of scalable, self-directed creativity, where content fuels identity, influence, and entrepreneurship.

data.title: ASHLEY GIBSON BARNETT MUSEUM OF ART AT FLORIDA SOUTHERN COLLEGE PRESENTS LIFE: SIX WOMEN PHOTOGRAPHERS
data.description:
ASHLEY GIBSON BARNETT MUSEUM OF ART AT FLORIDA SOUTHERN COLLEGE PRESENTS LIFE: SIX WOMEN PHOTOGRAPHERS

ASHLEY GIBSON BARNETT MUSEUM OF ART AT FLORIDA SOUTHERN COLLEGE PRESENTS LIFE: SIX WOMEN PHOTOGRAPHERS

PR Newswire

LAKELAND, Fla., Nov. 20, 2026

LAKELAND, Fla., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Ashley Gibson Barnett Museum of Art (The AGB) at Florida Southern College is proud to present LIFE: Six Women Photographers, an exhibition celebrating six pioneering women whose groundbreaking work helped shape modern photojournalism and transformed how Americans experienced the world through photography. Featuring more than 70 photographs by Margaret Bourke-White, Marie Hansen, Martha Holmes, Lisa Larsen, Nina Leen and Hansel Mieth, the exhibition opened Nov. 14, 2026, and will remain on view through March 7, 2027.

The exhibition, organized by The New-York Historical Society, highlights the contributions of the only six women employed as full-time photographers by LIFE magazine between the late 1930s and early 1970s out of 101 photographers on staff during its run as a weekly publication. At a time when photojournalism was largely dominated by men, these photographers documented defining moments in American history, captured significant social and political changes, and brought compelling human stories to millions of readers.

"These six remarkable women helped shape the way generations of Americans experienced and understood the world through photography," said Dr. Daryl Ward, executive director of The AGB. "Their work not only documented pivotal moments in history but also challenged conventions in a profession where women were often overlooked. We are proud to bring this important exhibition to Central Florida and share their extraordinary contributions to photography and journalism with our community."

First presented in New York in 2019, the exhibition explores the way Americans saw the world through the lens of photographers at LIFE, the first magazine in the United States to tell stories with images rather than text. These innovative photo essays became the hallmark of the publication. The exhibition provides context to this unique storytelling format through published and unpublished photographs, including vintage prints, copy prints and contact sheets. In addition, the photographs show the editing process behind the final published stories that helped define the United States as a world power during what Henry Luce, LIFE founder and editor-in-chief, called the "American Century." This is the first exhibition to focus on the six women who worked as full-time photographers for LIFE.

LIFE: Six Women Photographers was curated by Marilyn Satin Kushner, former curator and head of the Department of Prints, Photographs, and Architectural Collections, as well as Sarah Gordon, curatorial scholar in women's history, with Erin Levitsky of Ryerson University and William J. Simmons, former Andrew Mellon Foundation Pre-Doctoral Fellow at the Center for Women's History.

The exhibition is proudly sponsored by Northern Trust. Generous support is provided by Joyce B. Cowin, with additional support from Lara Lee Schupf, Jerry Speyer, and Robert A.M. Stern. This exhibition has been organized by The New-York Historical Society.

LIFE is the registered trademark of TI Gotham Inc. Used under license.

data.title: Stocks could face a 'doom loop' if Wall Street underestimates the risk of an economic downturn, strategist warns
data.description:
By Steve Goldstein

Wall Street is underpricing the hard-landing risk, one Bank of America strategist says. Here's what investors should know.

A hard landing could trigger a "doom loop" for stocks, warns one Wall Street strategist.

The S&P 500 is nearing a level worth buying if the U.S. avoids a recession, but one strategist warns Wall Street is underpricing the risk of a hard landing, saying investors should wait before buying risky assets.

Strategists led by Michael Hartnett said if the Fed is still Wall Street's best friend and corporate credit and the S&P 500 continue to slide, market turmoil will "short-circuit" the Fed rate-hike cycle. But if the Fed is now an "inflation tough guy" after the midterms, the hard-landing risks grow.

Hartnett's comments come amid increasingly hawkish central-bank commentary, with St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem talking of the need for as many as four rate increases by the spring. Fed governor Christopher Waller has said the central bank should consider a half-point rate rise in December.

An S&P 500 SPX below 7,000, in a soft-landing scenario where the U.S. avoids a recession, would be a buy, he said.

The S&P 500 closed Thursday at 7,175.83, now more than 2% below its 200-day average. Stock-market futures (ES00) pointed to a weaker start on Friday.

Bank of America's own fund-manager survey, released Tuesday, showed half the investors they polled thought there would be a soft landing and 42% expected no landing at all, i.e. continued or accelerating growth. Only 3% expected a recession. "We say hard landing likelihood too low," said Hartnett.

He said he fears a doom loop, where once estimates of GDP and earnings per share are reduced, stock-market allocations are cut, and investors only sell what they own. For now, investors are "hiding" in low-volatility and defensive stocks, he said.

Investors should wait until the narrative flips from Fed hikes to Fed cuts, then buy "cyclicals Cs" - crypto, chips, copper, consumer and condos.

-Steve Goldstein
